items.title: Board memo: Pause on onboarding digital-asset clients
items.text:
To: Board Risk Committee
From: Catherine Hale, Chief Executive Officer
Date: August 20, 2026
Re: Pause on onboarding new clients whose wealth derives from digital assets

Recommendation
I recommend that the committee approve a pause on onboarding new clients whose wealth derives from digital assets, effective Saturday, August 22, 2026. The pause applies to new relationships across Wealth Management and Lending. Existing clients, including those with digital-asset holdings or history, are unaffected and will continue to be serviced and monitored under current procedures.

Background
On July 28 the Office of Financial Supervision sent a supervisory letter to our Chief Compliance Officer highlighting its new interim guidance on onboarding clients with crypto-derived wealth. The letter makes clear that OFS expects firms to show AML controls that can evidence source of funds and source of wealth for these clients, not simply collect attestations. OFS has said final guidance will follow but has not given a date.

In response, Marcus Bell opened Compliance assessment COMP-112 on August 4. The assessment, with analysis from Nadia Petrov, found that AMLMonitor cannot trace on-chain flows. AMLMonitor draws on DataLake and FraudScore, neither of which ingests blockchain data, and we have no blockchain analytics vendor under contract. As a result we cannot independently verify where a prospect's digital-asset wealth came from before it reaches us as fiat. At the time of the assessment, nine active wealth prospects fell into this category.

Risk Considerations
Owen Gallagher and the Risk team have raised separate concerns about custody and counterparty exposure to crypto custodians and exchanges, including concentration with a small number of providers and limited recourse in a failure. Owen has also asked, rightly, what our exit plan would be if OFS tightens its guidance after we have taken clients on. Today we do not have a good answer.

Commercial Considerations
The #crypto-policy working group has had a full and useful debate. Grace Lin has made a strong case for continuing: Wealth Management sees 14 prospects in the broader pipeline representing roughly $40M of potential AUM, and competitors are onboarding these clients. She proposed an enhanced due diligence approach as a bridge. Martin Osei weighed that revenue against the regulatory exposure and suggested this committee make the call. I take the commercial point seriously, but enhanced due diligence without on-chain tracing still leaves us unable to evidence source of funds, which is precisely what OFS has flagged.

Conditions for Lifting the Pause
I propose the pause be lifted when both of the following are met:
(a) A blockchain analytics capability is integrated into AMLMonitor so that Compliance can trace on-chain flows as part of onboarding and ongoing monitoring.
(b) OFS publishes its final guidance on digital-asset client onboarding, so that our controls can be tested against the final standard rather than interim expectations.
Compliance will report back to this committee when both conditions are satisfied, with a recommendation on the enhanced due diligence framework to apply on resumption.

Next Steps
If approved, Grace will brief the wealth advisors, Brian Kowalski will brief Lending, and Compliance will ask relationship managers to hold any in-flight onboarding of affected prospects. Technology will scope the AMLMonitor integration with Compliance in parallel so we are ready to move once a vendor is selected.

Catherine

items.title: Board risk committee - digital-asset clients
items.text:
Catherine Hale: Okay, let's start. Everyone has the memo I circulated last night. The proposal is a pause on onboarding new clients whose wealth derives from digital assets, effective tomorrow, August 22. Marcus, can you give the short version of COMP-112 first?
Marcus Bell: Sure. The OFS letter from July 28 says, in effect, show us you can evidence source of funds for crypto-derived wealth. Nadia's work on COMP-112 confirmed AMLMonitor can't trace on-chain flows. It sees fiat once it hits us through DataLake and FraudScore, but nothing before that. No blockchain analytics vendor, no on-chain data. So any attestation we take from a prospect, we can't test.
Catherine Hale: Owen, the custody side.
Owen Gallagher: Two points. Counterparty exposure to the custodians these clients use is concentrated in a handful of names, and our recourse if one fails is thin. And the exit question I raised in the channel: if final guidance comes out stricter than the interim, we'd be offboarding clients we just brought on. That's reputational damage and operational cost.
Catherine Hale: Grace, I want your view on the record.
Grace Lin: I'll be direct, I disagree with the pause. We have 14 prospects in the pipeline, about $40M of AUM, and nine of them are far along. Competitors are taking these clients now. An enhanced due diligence process with wallet attestations, exchange statements, tax records, would let us keep going while we find a vendor.
Marcus Bell: I understand that, Grace, and the documents help. But exchange statements show balances, not provenance. Without tracing we can't evidence where the coins came from, and that's the specific gap OFS called out.
Martin Osei: From the finance side, $40M of AUM is real but it's run-rate fee revenue in the low hundreds of thousands. One adverse exam finding costs us more than that in remediation and management time. I'm comfortable with a pause as long as it's clearly temporary and tied to conditions.
Linda Brandt: Operationally, what happens to the nine in flight?
Marcus Bell: We'd ask the RMs to hold them at the current step in KYCPipeline. Nothing gets declined, it just doesn't progress. We tell the prospect we're finalizing our framework.
Linda Brandt: Good. I'd want Technology scoping the AMLMonitor integration now rather than after a vendor is chosen. Sam's team can look at how on-chain data lands alongside the DataLake feeds.
Grace Lin: If we pause, I want the lifting conditions concrete. I don't want this drifting for a year.
Catherine Hale: Agreed. Two conditions in the memo. One, blockchain analytics integrated into AMLMonitor. Two, OFS publishes final guidance. Both, not either. Existing clients are unaffected.
Owen Gallagher: I'd add that on resumption we revisit custody limits, but that doesn't need to be a condition.
Catherine Hale: Fair, we'll take that as part of the resumption recommendation. Marcus, you own reporting back to this committee when both conditions are met.
Marcus Bell: Will do. I'll have Nadia run vendor evaluations in parallel so we're not starting from zero.
Catherine Hale: Let's vote. Pause on onboarding new digital-asset-derived clients effective August 22, lifting when both conditions are met, existing clients unaffected. Martin?
Martin Osei: Approve.
Linda Brandt: Approve.
Owen Gallagher: Approve.
Marcus Bell: Approve.
Grace Lin: I'll note my disagreement for the minutes, but I accept the decision and I'll communicate it to the team. Approve.
Catherine Hale: Thank you, Grace, that's appreciated. Motion carries. Grace briefs wealth advisors Monday, Linda will make sure Lending hears it from Brian. Thanks all.

items.title: Pause on new digital-asset clients
items.text:
Hi team,

Following the board risk committee decision on Friday, August 21, onboarding of new clients whose wealth derives from digital assets is paused, effective Saturday, August 22.

What this means in practice:
- Do not open or progress new relationships where crypto is a material source of wealth. If a prospect is already in KYCPipeline, leave them at their current step; Compliance will hold the file.
- Existing clients are unaffected. Keep servicing them as normal.
- With prospects, keep it simple: we are finalizing our framework for digital-asset wealth and will be back in touch. Please don't speculate on timing.

The pause lifts once blockchain analytics is live in AMLMonitor and OFS publishes final guidance. I argued for continuing, but the decision is made and I'm behind it.

Any questions on specific prospects, route them to Compliance (Marcus or Nadia) and copy me.

Thanks,
Grace

items.title: Recommendation: resume digital-asset client onboarding
items.text:
Catherine, Grace,

I'm writing to confirm that both conditions the board risk committee set on August 21 for lifting the pause have now been met:

1. OFS published its final guidance on digital-asset client onboarding on October 5. Nadia and I have reviewed it against our draft framework; it largely tracks the interim guidance, with a firmer expectation on ongoing monitoring rather than onboarding-only checks.
2. ChainSight blockchain analytics went live inside AMLMonitor on October 6. On-chain tracing results now sit alongside the existing DataLake and FraudScore inputs, and alerts route through the normal AMLMonitor queues. Same day, KYCPipeline ownership moved to Compliance, so the onboarding steps and the screening sit under one team.

My recommendation is that we resume onboarding of clients with crypto-derived wealth effective Monday, October 12, 2026, under enhanced due diligence:
- Source-of-funds tracing via ChainSight for all declared wallets before account opening, with Compliance sign-off on any high-risk exposure.
- Quarterly reviews for these relationships for at least the first year, which also addresses the ongoing-monitoring point in the final guidance.

Owen, I'd still like your team's view on custody concentration limits as part of the first quarterly cycle.

This supersedes the August 22 pause. If you're both comfortable, Grace can brief the advisors and we'll release the held files in KYCPipeline on the 12th.

Marcus

Approved. Digital-asset onboarding resumes Monday Oct 12 under the enhanced due diligence Marcus laid out (ChainSight source-of-funds tracing, quarterly reviews). Grace, can you brief the advisors before then? Thanks all for getting both conditions over the line.
